title: Integral constructibility under continuous section encoding
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l in the scheme universe, K a small finite normed extension of Q_l, and X a noetherian scheme. Use the continuous coefficient rings and explicit internal/sectionwise module encodings of [def-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-module-encoding]. Given any isomorphism c from the continuous O_E coefficient sheaf to the continuous O_K coefficient sheaf on X, and an internal module M over the pulled-back continuous O_K condensed ring, assume M is constructible in the stratified local-finite-presentation sense. Then its continuous integer section encoding, followed by scalar transport along c, is constructible in the finite scalar-model sense of [def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module]. No rational scalar extension or lattice-existence hypothesis or conclusion occurs.

proof.text: Postcompose continuous functions with the valuation-ring equivalence between WithAbs E and E. This gives an isomorphism of the condensed integral point rings. The integral local-finite-presentation/constant-model comparison and invariance under coefficient isomorphism identify constructible internal modules over the derived integer coefficient ring with modules admitting stratified finite scalar models.

proof.text: Choose the uniquely normalized completed section-ring comparison and the normalized continuous integral coefficient comparison. Compose these with the supplied coefficient-sheaf isomorphism and the continuous chart comparison to obtain an isomorphism from the derived integer coefficient ring to the internal coefficient ring of M. Comap M along this isomorphism; it remains constructible. Apply the previous step and the existing integral section local-model theorem.

proof.text: The section-action module obtained in step 2 is isomorphic to the continuous encoding in the statement transported to completed coefficients. The isomorphism is the identity on each section; scalar compatibility follows from the normalized section-ring comparison, inverse equations for the coefficient isomorphisms, and the section/comap comparison. Transport the stratified finite models along this isomorphism. The essentially-small-site section-action instances provide the monoidal sheaf structure, with the site size fixed explicitly.

proof.text: On each stratum use the normalized integral slice-model comparison to turn completed constant models into continuous scalar-extension models. Replace covering sieves by their generating covering families and keep the same finite stratification. This is exactly continuous constructibility. Empty covers and zero presentations are preserved.

theorem integralContinuousEncoding_constructible
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (K : Type) [NormedField K] [NormedAlgebra ℚ_[l] K]
    [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] K] (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (c : latticeCoefficientSheaf X (latticeCoefficientIntegers l E) ≅
      lisseIntegerSheaf l K X)
    (M : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj (CondensedRing.integralCoeff l K) X))
    (hM : IsConstructibleModuleObject
      (condensedRingObj (CondensedRing.integralCoeff l K) X) M) :
    IsContinuousConstructible X (latticeCoefficientIntegers l E)
      ((CondensedRing.ringModuleEquivalenceOfIso X
        ((sheafCompose (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
          (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).mapIso c)).functor.obj
        ((CondensedRing.continuousIntegerModuleEquivalence l K X).functor.obj M))
